*** Add File: metaverse-ui-assets/README.md
+# Metaverse UI Asset Series
+
+This folder is a curated local subset copied from `cc0-game-assets-library`.
+It keeps complete asset packs intact so each pack still includes its preview,
+license file, spritesheets, tilemaps, and original folder structure.
+
+## Recommended Core Style
+
+Use these as the main visual language for a 2D metaverse MVP:
+
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-rpg-urban-pack`: modern top-down city roads, buildings, props, and urban map parts.
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-tiny-town`: compact town buildings, roads, trees, shops, fences, and scenery props.
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-rpg-base`: grass, water, buildings, characters, icons, and base RPG map pieces.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-ui-pack-sci-fi`: panels, buttons, sci-fi UI frames, and fonts for wallet, inventory, and dashboard screens.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-minimap-pack`: minimap tiles, markers, arrows, and navigation overlays.
+- `04-avatars-and-social/kenney-emotes-pack`: emotes, dialogue reactions, and social feedback.
+- `06-input-and-mobile-controls/kenney-input-prompts`: keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad prompts.
+- `07-vfx-lighting-and-portals/kenney-particle-pack`: particles for portals, rewards, magic, and UI feedback.
+
+## Folder Use
+
+- `00-manifest`: source catalog CSV files copied from the parent asset library.
+- `01-world-and-land`: world overview maps, land-grid concepts, territory and island systems.
+- `02-city-and-buildings`: main walkable town/city map tiles and building props.
+- `03-sci-fi-and-space`: space station, planet, UFO, spaceship, and future-zone assets.
+- `04-avatars-and-social`: avatar/NPC bases, robot characters, emotes, and social state graphics.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons`: HUD, wallet, inventory, minimap, feature icons, and item icons.
+- `06-input-and-mobile-controls`: keyboard/gamepad/touch prompts and mobile virtual control<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="728" />i-Fi,05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-ui-pack-sci-fi,wallet inventory dashboard panels buttons and fonts,core

+# GameGmeta
+
+GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.
+
+The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into
+a usable 2D virtual-world prototype: city map, land plots, avatar/social UI,
+wallet/inventory panels, minimap navigation, and portal effects.
+
+## Project Structure
+
+- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
+- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
+- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
+- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.
+
+## Local Asset Source
+
+The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`
+
+This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
+yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
+runtime asset pipeline are fixed.
+
+## Core Visual Direction
+
+Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:
+
+- modern city and small town maps
+- world/land overview maps
+- simple avatar and robot NPCs
+- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
+- minimap and input prompts
+- portal, reward, and lighting effects
+
+Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
+packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.
+

+# GameGmeta Product Brief
+
+## Concept
+
+GameGmeta is a lightweight 2D metaverse prototype focused on map-based social
+interaction and MetaAI-assisted world building.
+
+Players enter a top-down virtual city, move between districts, inspect land
+plots, open wallet/inventory panels, react with emotes, and interact with
+portals that connect city, space, and event zones.
+
+## MVP Scope
+
+- Top-down city lobby using `kenney-rpg-urban-pack`, `kenney-tiny-town`, and
+  `kenney-rpg-base<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="137" />endering.
+- Mixed visual styles from unrelated asset packs.
+
+## Asset Rule
+
+Keep source CC0 licenses next to copied asset packs. If production code imports
+actual image files into this repo later, copy the relevant pack's `License.txt`
+and source URL note with the imported files.
+

+# GameGmeta
+
+GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.
+
+The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into
+a usable 2D virtual-world prototype: city map, land plots, avatar/social UI,
+wallet/inventory panels, minimap navigation, and portal effects.
+
+## Project Structure
+
+- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
+- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
+- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
+- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.
+
+## Local Asset Source
+
+The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`
+
+This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
+yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
+runtime asset pipeline are fixed.
+
+## Core Visual Direction
+
+Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:
+
+- modern city and small town maps
+- world/land overview maps
+- simple avatar and robot NPCs
+- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
+- minimap and input prompts
+- portal, reward, and lighting effects
+
+Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
+packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.
+

+# GameGmeta Product Brief
+
+## Concept
+
+GameGmeta is a lightweight 2D metaverse prototype focused on map-based social
+interaction and MetaAI-assisted world building.
+
+Players enter a top-down virtual city, move between districts, inspect land
+plots, open wallet/inventory panels, react with emotes, and interact with
+portals that connect city, space, and event zones.
+
+## MVP Scope
+
+- Top-down city lobby using `kenney-rpg-urban-pack`, `kenney-tiny-town`, and
+  `kenney-rpg-base<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="137" />endering.
+- Mixed visual styles from unrelated asset packs.
+
+## Asset Rule
+
+Keep source CC0 licenses next to copied asset packs. If production code imports
+actual image files into this repo later, copy the relevant pack's `License.txt`
+and source URL note with the imported files.
+

+
+This folder is a curated local subset copied from `cc0-game-assets-library`.

+# GameGmeta
+
+GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.
+
+The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into
+a usable 2D virtual-world prototype: city map, land plots, avatar/social UI,
+wallet/inventory panels, minimap navigation, and portal effects.
+
+## Project Structure
+
+- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
+- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
+- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
+- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.
+
+## Local Asset Source
+
+The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`
+
+This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
+yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
+runtime asset pipeline are fixed.
+
+## Core Visual Direction
+
+Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:
+
+- modern city and small town maps
+- world/land overview maps
+- simple avatar and robot NPCs
+- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
+- minimap and input prompts
+- portal, reward, and lighting effects
+
+Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
+packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.
+
*** Add File: GameGmeta/docs/product-brief.md
+# GameGmeta Product Brief
+
+## Concept
+
+GameGmeta is a lightweight 2D metaverse prototype focused on map-based social
+interaction and MetaAI-assisted world building.
+
+Players enter a top-down virtual city, move between districts, inspect land
+plots, open wallet/inventory panels, react with emotes, and interact with
+portals that connect city, space, and event zones.
+
+## MVP Scope
+
+- Top-down city lobby using `kenney-rpg-urban-pack`, `kenney-tiny-town`, and
+  `kenney-rpg-base<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="137" />endering.
+- Mixed visual styles from unrelated asset packs.
+
+## Asset Rule
+
+Keep source CC0 licenses next to copied asset packs. If production code imports
+actual image files into this repo later, copy the relevant pack's `License.txt`
+and source URL note with the imported files.
+

+
+## Canonical Local Source
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`

+## Selected Manifest
+

+## Recommended First Scene Assets

*** Add File: metaverse-ui-assets/README.md
+# Metaverse UI Asset Series
+
+This folder is a curated local subset copied from `cc0-game-assets-library`.
+It keeps complete asset packs intact so each pack still includes its preview,
+license file, spritesheets, tilemaps, and original folder structure.
+
+## Recommended Core Style
+
+Use these as the main visual language for a 2D metaverse MVP:
+
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-rpg-urban-pack`: modern top-down city roads, buildings, props, and urban map parts.
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-tiny-town`: compact town buildings, roads, trees, shops, fences, and scenery props.
+- `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-rpg-base`: grass, water, buildings, characters, icons, and base RPG map pieces.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-ui-pack-sci-fi`: panels, buttons, sci-fi UI frames, and fonts for wallet, inventory, and dashboard screens.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-minimap-pack`: minimap tiles, markers, arrows, and navigation overlays.
+- `04-avatars-and-social/kenney-emotes-pack`: emotes, dialogue reactions, and social feedback.
+- `06-input-and-mobile-controls/kenney-input-prompts`: keyboard, mouse, touch, and gamepad prompts.
+- `07-vfx-lighting-and-portals/kenney-particle-pack`: particles for portals, rewards, magic, and UI feedback.
+
+## Folder Use
+
+- `00-manifest`: source catalog CSV files copied from the parent asset library.
+- `01-world-and-land`: world overview maps, land-grid concepts, territory and island systems.
+- `02-city-and-buildings`: main walkable town/city map tiles and building props.
+- `03-sci-fi-and-space`: space station, planet, UFO, spaceship, and future-zone assets.
+- `04-avatars-and-social`: avatar/NPC bases, robot characters, emotes, and social state graphics.
+- `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons`: HUD, wallet, inventory, minimap, feature icons, and item icons.

*** Add File: GameGmeta/README.md
+# GameGmeta
+
+GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.
+
+The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into
+a usable 2D virtual-world prototype: city map, land plots, avatar/social UI,
+wallet/inventory panels, minimap navigation, and portal effects.
+
+## Project Structure
+
+- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
+- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
+- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
+- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.
+
+## Local Asset Source
+
+The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`
+
+This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
+yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
+runtime asset pipeline are fixed.
+
+## Core Visual Direction
+
+Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:
+
+- modern city and small town maps
+- world/land overview maps
+- simple avatar and robot NPCs
+- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
+- minimap and input prompts
+- portal, reward, and lighting effects
+
+Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
+packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.
+
*** Add File: GameGmeta/docs/product-brief.md
+# GameGmeta Product Brief
+
+## Concept
+
+GameGmeta is a lightweight 2D metaverse prototype focused on map-based social
+interaction and MetaAI-assisted world building.
+
+Players enter a top-down virtual city, move between districts, inspect land
+plots, open wallet/inventory panels, react with emotes, and interact with
+portals that connect city, space, and event zones.
+
+## MVP Scope
+
+- Top-down city lobby using `kenney-rpg-urban-pack`, `kenney-tiny-town`, and
+  `kenney-rpg-base<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="137" />endering.
+- Mixed visual styles from unrelated asset packs.
+
+## Asset Rule
+
+Keep source CC0 licenses next to copied asset packs. If production code imports
+actual image files into this repo later, copy the relevant pack's `License.txt`
+and source URL note with the imported files.
+
*** Add File: GameGmeta/docs/asset-usage.md
+# Asset Usage
+
+## Canonical Local Source
+
+`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`
+
+## Selected Manifest
+
+`assets/manifests/selected-metaverse-assets.csv`
+
+## Import Strategy
+
+1. Prototype against the external curated source folder.
+2. Once the engine is chosen, copy only the images needed by the first playable
+   scene into the project.
+3. Preserve package names in imported paths so provenance remains clear.
+4. Keep `License.txt` and source URLs alongside copied production assets.
+
+## Recommended First Scene Assets
+
+- City tiles: `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-rpg-urban-pack`
+- Town props: `02-city-and-buildings/kenney-tiny-town`
+- UI panels: `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-ui-pack-sci-fi`
+- Minimap: `05-ui-hud-wallet-and-icons/kenney-minimap-pack`
+- Emotes: `04-avatars-and-social/kenney-emotes-pack`
+- Input prompts: `06-input-and-mobile-controls/kenney-input-prompts`
+- Portal effects: `07-vfx-lighting-and-portals/kenney-particle-pack`

+const TILE := 32

+const MAP_W := 46

+const PLAYER_SPEED := 210.0
+

+const TOWN_ATLAS := "res://assets/game/tiles/tiny_town_tilemap.png"
+const SCIFI_ATLAS := "res://assets/game/tiles/scifi_tilesheet.png"
+const AVATAR_SHEET := "res://assets/game/avatars/shape_characters.png"
+const ROBOT_SHEET := "res://assets/game/avatars/robots_top.png"
+const EMOTE_SHEET := "res://assets/game/avatars/emotes_pixel.png"
+const PORTAL_MAGIC := "res://assets/game/vfx/portal_magic.png"
+const SPARK := "res://assets/game/vfx/spark.png"
+const PLANET := "res://assets/game/space/planet_sphere.png"

+var player: Node2D
+var camera: Camera2D
+var status_label: Label
+var zone_label: Label

+var poi_list: Array[Dictionary] = []
+var map_origin := Vector2.ZERO
+
+func _ready() -> void:
+	get_viewport().canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
+	_build_world()
+	_build_pois()
+	_build_player()
+	_build_hud()
+	_update_status("Meta City online. Move with WASD / arrows. Press E near a district.")
+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_handle_movement(delta)
+	_animate_portals(delta)
+	_update_nearest_zone()
+	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("interact"):
+		_interact()
+
+func _build_world() -> void:
+	_add_background()
+	var ground := Node2D.new()
+	ground.name = "PixelMap"
+	add_child(ground)
+	_draw_ground_tiles(ground)
+	_draw_city_roads(ground)
+	_draw_district_blocks(ground)
+	_draw_sci_fi_zone(ground)
+	_draw_land_preview(ground)
+	_draw_border(ground)
+<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="2577" /> = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
+	parent.add_child(sprite)
+	return sprite
+
+func _stamp(parent: Node2D, atlas_path: String, origin: Vector2i, coords: Array[Vector2i], z: int) -> void:
+	var i := 0
+	for y in 2:
+		for x in 2:
+			var coord := coords[i]
+			_add_tile(parent, _atlas(atlas_path, coord.x, coord.y), origin.x + x, origin.y + y, z)
+			i += 1
+
+func _add_portal_marker(pos: Vector2) -> void:
+	var portal := Sprite2D.new()
+	portal.name = "PortalMarker"
+	portal.texture = _texture(PORTAL_MAGIC)
+	portal.position = pos
+	portal.scale = Vector2(0.42, 0.42)
+	portal.modulate = Color(0.25, 0.9, 1.0, 0.72)
+	portal.z_index = 12
+	portal_sprites.append(portal)
+	add_child(portal)
+
+func _add_label(text: String, pos: Vector2, color: Color) -> void:
+	var label := Label.new()
+	label.text = text
+	label.position = pos
+	label.z_index = 30
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_shadow_color", Color(0, 0, 0, 0.7))
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_x", 2)
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_y", 2)
+	label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	add_child(label)
+
+func _atlas(path: String, col: int, row: int) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var x := col * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	var y := row * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	return _atlas_custom(path, Rect2(x, y, SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE))
+
+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var texture := load(path) as Texture2D
+	if texture == null:
+		push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture
*** End Patch

+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_handle_movement(delta)
+	_animate_portals(delta)
+	_update_nearest_zone()

+		_interact()

+func _build_world() -> void:
+	_add_background()

+	ground.name = "PixelMap"
+	add_child(ground)
+	_draw_ground_tiles(ground)
+	_draw_city_roads(ground)
+	_draw_district_blocks(ground)
+	_draw_sci_fi_zone(ground)
+	_draw_land_preview(ground)
+	_draw_border(ground)

+func _stamp(parent: Node2D, atlas_path: String, origin: Vector2i, coords: Array[Vector2i], z: int) -> void:
+	var i := 0
+	for y in 2:
+		for x in 2:
+			var coord := coords[i]
+			_add_tile(parent, _atlas(atlas_path, coord.x, coord.y), origin.x + x, origin.y + y, z)
+			i += 1
+
+func _add_portal_marker(pos: Vector2) -> void:
+	var portal := Sprite2D.new()
+	portal.name = "PortalMarker"
+	portal.texture = _texture(PORTAL_MAGIC)
+	portal.position = pos
+	portal.scale = Vector2(0.42, 0.42)
+	portal.modulate = Color(0.25, 0.9, 1.0, 0.72)
+	portal.z_index = 12
+	portal_sprites.append(portal)
+	add_child(portal)
+
+func _add_label(text: String, pos: Vector2, color: Color) -> void:
+	var label := Label.new()
+	label.text = text
+	label.position = pos
+	label.z_index = 30
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_shadow_color", Color(0, 0, 0, 0.7))
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_x", 2)
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_y", 2)
+	label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	add_child(label)
+
+func _atlas(path: String, col: int, row: int) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var x := col * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	var y := row * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	return _atlas_custom(path, Rect2(x, y, SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE))
+
+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var texture := load(path) as Texture2D
+	if texture == null:
+		push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture

+	get_viewport().canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST

+
+func _process(delta: float) -> void:
+	_handle_movement(delta)
+	_animate_portals(delta)
+	_update_nearest_zone()
+	if Input.is_action_just_pressed("interact"):
+		_interact()
+
+func _build_world() -> void:
+	_add_background()
+	var ground := Node2D.new()
+	ground.name = "PixelMap"
+	add_child(ground)
+	_draw_ground_tiles(ground)
+	_draw_city_roads(ground)
+	_draw_district_blocks(ground)
+	_draw_sci_fi_zone(ground)
+	_draw_land_preview(ground)
+	_draw_border(ground)
+<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="2577" /> = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST
+	parent.add_child(sprite)
+	return sprite

+func _stamp(parent: Node2D, atlas_path: String, origin: Vector2i, coords: Array[Vector2i], z: int) -> void:
+	var i := 0
+	for y in 2:
+		for x in 2:
+			var coord := coords[i]
+			_add_tile(parent, _atlas(atlas_path, coord.x, coord.y), origin.x + x, origin.y + y, z)
+			i += 1
+
+func _add_portal_marker(pos: Vector2) -> void:
+	var portal := Sprite2D.new()
+	portal.name = "PortalMarker"
+	portal.texture = _texture(PORTAL_MAGIC)
+	portal.position = pos
+	portal.scale = Vector2(0.42, 0.42)
+	portal.modulate = Color(0.25, 0.9, 1.0, 0.72)
+	portal.z_index = 12
+	portal_sprites.append(portal)
+	add_child(portal)
+
+func _add_label(text: String, pos: Vector2, color: Color) -> void:
+	var label := Label.new()
+	label.text = text
+	label.position = pos
+	label.z_index = 30
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)
+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_shadow_color", Color(0, 0, 0, 0.7))
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_x", 2)
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_y", 2)
+	label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	add_child(label)
+
+func _atlas(path: String, col: int, row: int) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var x := col * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	var y := row * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	return _atlas_custom(path, Rect2(x, y, SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE))
+
+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var texture := load(path) as Texture2D
+	if texture == null:
+		push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture

+	label.add_theme_color_override("font_shadow_color", Color(0, 0, 0, 0.7))
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_x", 2)
+	label.add_theme_constant_override("shadow_offset_y", 2)
+	label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 14)
+	add_child(label)
+
+func _atlas(path: String, col: int, row: int) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var x := col * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	var y := row * (SOURCE_TILE + ATLAS_SPACING)
+	return _atlas_custom(path, Rect2(x, y, SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE))
+
+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):

+	var texture := load(path) as Texture2D
+	if texture == null:

+	atlas_cache[path] = texture

name: frontend-app-builder
description: Use for new frontend applications, dashboards, games, creative websites, hero sections, and visually driven UI from scratch, or when the user explicitly asks for a redesign/restyle/modernization. Builds from clean, airy, high-taste, readable image-generated concept design with section-specific references, faithful implementation, and browser testing.
---

# Frontend App Builder

Use this skill to create polished frontend apps, dashboards, games, creative websites, hero sections, redesigns, and other visually driven UI. Act first as a senior front-end designer, then as an engineer implementing an approved design spec.

## Core Standard

The two priorities of this skill outrank everything else:

1. Create enough great-looking Image Gen design first: clean, airy, distinctive, complete, readable, section-specific when needed, and not repetitive by default.
2. Do not stop until the accepted design and browser implementation match 10/10. Keep fixing visual, interaction, responsive, asset, and typography mismatches until `view_image` comparison would pass agency sign-off.

## Hard Rules

1. Use Image Gen for the visual concept unless the user explicitly opts out or the task is a small UI fix inside an existing design system.
2. Design the complete requested surface before coding. For a full page, app, dashboard, game, or product interface, a header or hero concept is not enough. For multi-section websites and long landing pages, prefer coordinated section-by-section concepts, plus an optional overview for rhythm, over one tall image that loses detail. For apps, dashboards, games, or compact product surfaces, generate the full primary screen plus any needed state, responsive, or asset concepts first.
3. Inside Codex, default multi-section website concepting to one fresh, large, read<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="5040" />ature imagery.
- Product/SaaS pages: preserve product mockups, workflow diagrams, feature strips, proof elements, and brand treatment.
- Dashboards/tools: preserve density, sidebars, headers, tables, tabs, timelines, charts, maps, row counts, and selected/detail behavior. Do not turn table-driven concepts into card grids.
- Canvas/editor tools: preserve default zoom/pan, canvas/document text scale, chrome density, toolbars, sidebars, inspector controls, layer rows, status bars, command surfaces, and autosaved/seed-state behavior.
- Timeline/planning tools: preserve grid/time-axis anatomy, row spans, event density, status rails, and command-center fit.
- Clone-like interfaces: preserve the recognizable skeleton before adding polish. Do not add marketing heroes or custom navigation that breaks the product type.
- Games: preserve the art direction with Image Gen assets for sprites, tiles/platforms, collectibles, hazards, goals/checkpoints, props, and background/parallax layers. Verify assets load, scale, animate or swap state correctly, align with collision geometry, and support movement, action/jump/drag behavior, scoring, hazards, and restart.
- Media surfaces: verify real media load, duration, play/pause, seek/progress, and visible frame changes.
- Forms/booking/purchase/restaurant flows: verify the main transaction path and confirmation state.

## Final Response

Include the accepted concept path, rendered screenshot method, Browser/IAB verification method or Playwright fallback reason, `view_image` inspection of the accepted concept and latest implementation screenshot, native-size viewport checked or blocker, at least five inspected comparison points, above-the-fold copy diff result, remaining intentional deviations, and an explicit statement that the implementation was faithfully verified against the accepted design. Also include material mismatches fixed and core interaction path verified. If no material mismatches remain, say so directly.

name: web-game-foundations
description: Set browser-game architecture before implementation. Use when the user needs engine choice, simulation and render boundaries, input model, asset organization, or save/debug/performance strategy.
---

# Web Game Foundations

## Overview

Use this skill to establish the non-negotiable architecture before implementation starts. Browser games degrade quickly when simulation, rendering, UI, asset loading, and input handling are mixed together.

Default rule: simulation state is owned outside the renderer, browser UI is not forced into the canvas unless there is a clear reason, and shipped 3D assets default to GLB or glTF 2.0 rather than ad hoc model formats.

## Use This Skill When

- the user has not settled the engine or renderer choice
- the task is about boundaries, module shape, state ownership, or asset policy
- multiple specialist skills need one shared architectural frame

## Do Not Stay Here When

- the runtime track is clearly Phaser
- the runtime track is clearly vanilla Three.js
- the runtime track is clearly React Three Fiber
- the task is purely about shipped 3D assets

Once the stack is clear, hand off to the runtime or asset specialist skill.

## Architecture Rules

1. Separate simulation from rendering.
   - Simulation owns entities, turns, timers, collisions, progression, and saveable state.
   - The renderer owns scene composition, animation playback, camera, particles, and input plumbing.
2. Keep input mapping explicit.
   - Define actions such as `move`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `ability-1`, and `pause`.
   - Map physical inputs to actions in one place.
3. Treat asset loading as a first-class system.
   - Use stable manifest keys.
   - Group by domain: characters, environment, UI, audio, FX.
   - For 3D content, standardize on GLB or glTF 2.0 unless the chosen engine ecosystem requires a<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="175" />ser for 2D games with sprites, tilemaps, top-down or side-view action, turn-based grids, and classic browser arcade flows.
- Default to vanilla Three.js for explicit 3D scenes that want direct scene, camera, renderer, and loop control in plain TypeScript or Vite.
- Default to React Three Fiber when the 3D scene lives inside a React application and needs declarative composition, shared app state, or React-first UI coordination.
- Use raw WebGL only for shader-heavy or renderer-first projects where engine abstractions would get in the way.
- Keep Babylon.js and PlayCanvas as alternative-engine paths rather than the default code-generation target.

See `../../references/engine-selection.md` for the default decision table.

## Implementation Checklist

Define these before writing core code:

- Player fantasy and primary verbs
- Core loop and loss or reset states
- Camera model
- Input action map
- Simulation modules
- Renderer modules
- Asset manifest layout
- 3D asset format and optimization rules
- HUD and menu surfaces
- Save data boundary
- Debug and perf surfaces

## Anti-Patterns

- Mixing gameplay rules directly into scene callbacks
- Treating the renderer as the source of truth for game state
- Putting all HUD and menu UI into the canvas by default
- Letting asset filenames become the public API instead of manifest keys
- Shipping unoptimized 3D assets straight from the DCC tool into the browser
- Mixing camera-control state and menu or modal state without an explicit input boundary
- Rebuilding architecture every time the game changes genre

## References

- Engine selection: `../../references/engine-selection.md`
- Phaser structure: `../../references/phaser-architecture.md`
- Three.js structure: `../../references/three-webgl-architecture.md`
- Three.js ecosystem stack: `../../references/threejs-stack.md`
- React Three Fiber stack: `../../references/react-three-fiber-stack.md`
- 3D asset shipping: `../../references/web-3d-asset-pipeline.md`

name: game-ui-frontend
description: Design UI surfaces for browser games. Use when the user asks for HUDs, menus, overlays, responsive layouts, or visual direction that must protect the playfield.
---

# Game UI Frontend

## Overview

Use this skill whenever the game needs a visible interface layer. The job is not to produce generic dashboard UI. The job is to produce a readable, thematic browser-game interface that supports the play experience.

Default assumption: build the game world in canvas or WebGL, and build text-heavy UI in DOM.

## Frontend Standards

1. Establish visual direction before coding.
   - Genre and fantasy
   - Material language
   - Typography
   - Palette
   - Motion tone
2. Use CSS variables for the UI theme.
3. Build clear hierarchy.
   - Critical combat or survival information first
   - Secondary tools second
   - Rarely used settings behind menus or drawers
4. Protect the playfield first, especially in 3D.
   - The initial screen should feel playable within a few seconds.
   - Default to one primary persistent HUD cluster and at most one small secondary cluster.
   - Keep the center of the playfield clear during normal play.
   - Keep the lower-middle playfield mostly clear during normal play.
   - Put lore, field notes, quest details, and long control lists behind drawers, toggles, or pause surfaces.
   - Prefer contextual prompts and transient hints over permanent boxed panels.
5. Keep overlays readable over motion.
   - Use backing panels, edge treatment, contrast, and restrained blur where needed.
6. Design for both desktop and mobile from the start.
7. Design 3D UI around camera and input control boundaries.
   - Pause or gate camera-control input when menus, dialogs, or pointer-driven UI are active.
   - Keep pointer-lock, drag-to-look, and menu interaction states explicit.

## 3D Starter Defaults

For e<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="292" />oid

Use `../../references/frontend-prompts.md` for concrete prompt shapes.

## Motion Rules

- Prefer a few meaningful transitions over constant micro-animation.
- Reserve strong motion for state change, reward, danger, and onboarding.
- Respect reduced-motion settings for non-essential animation.
- Keep 3D HUD motion from competing with camera motion.

## What Good Looks Like

- HUD elements are legible without flattening the scene.
- Menus feel native to the game world, not like a SaaS admin panel.
- Layout adapts cleanly across breakpoints.
- Pointer, keyboard, and game-state feedback are obvious.
- In 3D games, menu and HUD states do not fight camera control or pointer-lock.
- In 3D games, the first playable view keeps most of the viewport available for movement, aiming, and spatial reading.
- Persistent information density is low enough that screenshots still read as game scenes, not UI comps.

## Anti-Patterns

- Generic app dashboard layouts
- Flat placeholder styling with no theme
- Default font stacks without intent
- Dense overlays that obscure the playfield
- Large title cards or multi-paragraph notes sitting over a live playable scene
- Equal-weight boxed panels distributed around every edge of the viewport
- Controls, objectives, notes, and lore all expanded at once on first load
- Full-width top-and-bottom chrome with large always-on center or body panels in 3D play
- Excessive motion on every element
- Canvas-only UI when DOM would be clearer and cheaper
- Forcing HUD controls into the 3D scene when standard DOM would be clearer
- Letting camera input remain active under modals or inventory panels

## References

- Shared architecture: `../web-game-foundations/SKILL.md`
- Prompt recipes: `../../references/frontend-prompts.md`
- Low-chrome 3D layout patterns: `../../references/three-hud-layout-patterns.md`
- React-hosted 3D UI context: `../react-three-fiber-game/SKILL.md`
- Playtest review: `../../references/playtest-checklist.md`

description: Use for new frontend applications, dashboards, games, creative websites, hero sections, and visually driven UI from scratch, or when the user explicitly asks for a redesign/restyle/modernization. Builds from clean, airy, high-taste, readable image-generated concept design with section-specific references, faithful implementation, and browser testing.

# Frontend App Builder

Use this skill to create polished frontend apps, dashboards, games, creative websites, hero sections, redesigns, and other visually driven UI. Act first as a senior front-end designer, then as an engineer implementing an approved design spec.

## Core Standard

The two priorities of this skill outrank everything else:

1. Create enough great-looking Image Gen design first: clean, airy, distinctive, complete, readable, section-specific when needed, and not repetitive by default.
2. Do not stop until the accepted design and browser implementation match 10/10. Keep fixing visual, interaction, responsive, asset, and typography mismatches until `view_image` comparison would pass agency sign-off.

## Hard Rules

1. Use Image Gen for the visual concept unless the user explicitly opts out or the task is a small UI fix inside an existing design system.
2. Design the complete requested surface before coding. For a full page, app, dashboard, game, or product interface, a header or hero concept is not enough. For multi-section websites and long landing pages, prefer coordinated section-by-section concepts, plus an optional overview for rhythm, over one tall image that loses detail. For apps, dashboards, games, or compact product surfaces, generate the full primary screen plus any needed state, responsive, or asset concepts first.
3. Inside Codex, default multi-section website concepting to one fresh, large, read<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="5040" />ature imagery.
- Product/SaaS pages: preserve product mockups, workflow diagrams, feature strips, proof elements, and brand treatment.
- Dashboards/tools: preserve density, sidebars, headers, tables, tabs, timelines, charts, maps, row counts, and selected/detail behavior. Do not turn table-driven concepts into card grids.
- Canvas/editor tools: preserve default zoom/pan, canvas/document text scale, chrome density, toolbars, sidebars, inspector controls, layer rows, status bars, command surfaces, and autosaved/seed-state behavior.
- Timeline/planning tools: preserve grid/time-axis anatomy, row spans, event density, status rails, and command-center fit.
- Clone-like interfaces: preserve the recognizable skeleton before adding polish. Do not add marketing heroes or custom navigation that breaks the product type.
- Games: preserve the art direction with Image Gen assets for sprites, tiles/platforms, collectibles, hazards, goals/checkpoints, props, and background/parallax layers. Verify assets load, scale, animate or swap state correctly, align with collision geometry, and support movement, action/jump/drag behavior, scoring, hazards, and restart.
- Media surfaces: verify real media load, duration, play/pause, seek/progress, and visible frame changes.
- Forms/booking/purchase/restaurant flows: verify the main transaction path and confirmation state.

## Final Response

Include the accepted concept path, rendered screenshot method, Browser/IAB verification method or Playwright fallback reason, `view_image` inspection of the accepted concept and latest implementation screenshot, native-size viewport checked or blocker, at least five inspected comparison points, above-the-fold copy diff result, remaining intentional deviations, and an explicit statement that the implementation was faithfully verified against the accepted design. Also include material mismatches fixed and core interaction path verified. If no material mismatches remain, say so directly.

name: web-game-foundations
description: Set browser-game architecture before implementation. Use when the user needs engine choice, simulation and render boundaries, input model, asset organization, or save/debug/performance strategy.
---

# Web Game Foundations

## Overview

Use this skill to establish the non-negotiable architecture before implementation starts. Browser games degrade quickly when simulation, rendering, UI, asset loading, and input handling are mixed together.

Default rule: simulation state is owned outside the renderer, browser UI is not forced into the canvas unless there is a clear reason, and shipped 3D assets default to GLB or glTF 2.0 rather than ad hoc model formats.

## Use This Skill When

- the user has not settled the engine or renderer choice
- the task is about boundaries, module shape, state ownership, or asset policy
- multiple specialist skills need one shared architectural frame

## Do Not Stay Here When

- the runtime track is clearly Phaser
- the runtime track is clearly vanilla Three.js
- the runtime track is clearly React Three Fiber
- the task is purely about shipped 3D assets

Once the stack is clear, hand off to the runtime or asset specialist skill.

## Architecture Rules

1. Separate simulation from rendering.
   - Simulation owns entities, turns, timers, collisions, progression, and saveable state.
   - The renderer owns scene composition, animation playback, camera, particles, and input plumbing.
2. Keep input mapping explicit.
   - Define actions such as `move`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `ability-1`, and `pause`.
   - Map physical inputs to actions in one place.
3. Treat asset loading as a first-class system.
   - Use stable manifest keys.
   - Group by domain: characters, environment, UI, audio, FX.
   - For 3D content, standardize on GLB or glTF 2.0 unless the chosen engine ecosystem requires a<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="175" />ser for 2D games with sprites, tilemaps, top-down or side-view action, turn-based grids, and classic browser arcade flows.
- Default to vanilla Three.js for explicit 3D scenes that want direct scene, camera, renderer, and loop control in plain TypeScript or Vite.
- Default to React Three Fiber when the 3D scene lives inside a React application and needs declarative composition, shared app state, or React-first UI coordination.
- Use raw WebGL only for shader-heavy or renderer-first projects where engine abstractions would get in the way.
- Keep Babylon.js and PlayCanvas as alternative-engine paths rather than the default code-generation target.

See `../../references/engine-selection.md` for the default decision table.

## Implementation Checklist

Define these before writing core code:

- Player fantasy and primary verbs
- Core loop and loss or reset states
- Camera model
- Input action map
- Simulation modules
- Renderer modules
- Asset manifest layout
- 3D asset format and optimization rules
- HUD and menu surfaces
- Save data boundary
- Debug and perf surfaces

## Anti-Patterns

- Mixing gameplay rules directly into scene callbacks
- Treating the renderer as the source of truth for game state
- Putting all HUD and menu UI into the canvas by default
- Letting asset filenames become the public API instead of manifest keys
- Shipping unoptimized 3D assets straight from the DCC tool into the browser
- Mixing camera-control state and menu or modal state without an explicit input boundary
- Rebuilding architecture every time the game changes genre

## References

- Engine selection: `../../references/engine-selection.md`
- Phaser structure: `../../references/phaser-architecture.md`
- Three.js structure: `../../references/three-webgl-architecture.md`
- Three.js ecosystem stack: `../../references/threejs-stack.md`
- React Three Fiber stack: `../../references/react-three-fiber-stack.md`
- 3D asset shipping: `../../references/web-3d-asset-pipeline.md`

name: game-ui-frontend
description: Design UI surfaces for browser games. Use when the user asks for HUDs, menus, overlays, responsive layouts, or visual direction that must protect the playfield.
---

# Game UI Frontend

## Overview

Use this skill whenever the game needs a visible interface layer. The job is not to produce generic dashboard UI. The job is to produce a readable, thematic browser-game interface that supports the play experience.

Default assumption: build the game world in canvas or WebGL, and build text-heavy UI in DOM.

## Frontend Standards

1. Establish visual direction before coding.
   - Genre and fantasy
   - Material language
   - Typography
   - Palette
   - Motion tone
2. Use CSS variables for the UI theme.
3. Build clear hierarchy.
   - Critical combat or survival information first
   - Secondary tools second
   - Rarely used settings behind menus or drawers
4. Protect the playfield first, especially in 3D.
   - The initial screen should feel playable within a few seconds.
   - Default to one primary persistent HUD cluster and at most one small secondary cluster.
   - Keep the center of the playfield clear during normal play.
   - Keep the lower-middle playfield mostly clear during normal play.
   - Put lore, field notes, quest details, and long control lists behind drawers, toggles, or pause surfaces.
   - Prefer contextual prompts and transient hints over permanent boxed panels.
5. Keep overlays readable over motion.
   - Use backing panels, edge treatment, contrast, and restrained blur where needed.
6. Design for both desktop and mobile from the start.
7. Design 3D UI around camera and input control boundaries.
   - Pause or gate camera-control input when menus, dialogs, or pointer-driven UI are active.
   - Keep pointer-lock, drag-to-look, and menu interaction states explicit.

## 3D Starter Defaults

For e<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="292" />oid

Use `../../references/frontend-prompts.md` for concrete prompt shapes.

## Motion Rules

- Prefer a few meaningful transitions over constant micro-animation.
- Reserve strong motion for state change, reward, danger, and onboarding.
- Respect reduced-motion settings for non-essential animation.
- Keep 3D HUD motion from competing with camera motion.

## What Good Looks Like

- HUD elements are legible without flattening the scene.
- Menus feel native to the game world, not like a SaaS admin panel.
- Layout adapts cleanly across breakpoints.
- Pointer, keyboard, and game-state feedback are obvious.
- In 3D games, menu and HUD states do not fight camera control or pointer-lock.
- In 3D games, the first playable view keeps most of the viewport available for movement, aiming, and spatial reading.
- Persistent information density is low enough that screenshots still read as game scenes, not UI comps.

## Anti-Patterns

- Generic app dashboard layouts
- Flat placeholder styling with no theme
- Default font stacks without intent
- Dense overlays that obscure the playfield
- Large title cards or multi-paragraph notes sitting over a live playable scene
- Equal-weight boxed panels distributed around every edge of the viewport
- Controls, objectives, notes, and lore all expanded at once on first load
- Full-width top-and-bottom chrome with large always-on center or body panels in 3D play
- Excessive motion on every element
- Canvas-only UI when DOM would be clearer and cheaper
- Forcing HUD controls into the 3D scene when standard DOM would be clearer
- Letting camera input remain active under modals or inventory panels

## References

- Shared architecture: `../web-game-foundations/SKILL.md`
- Prompt recipes: `../../references/frontend-prompts.md`
- Low-chrome 3D layout patterns: `../../references/three-hud-layout-patterns.md`
- React-hosted 3D UI context: `../react-three-fiber-game/SKILL.md`
- Playtest review: `../../references/playtest-checklist.md`

核心修改：GameGmeta 不再以“元宇宙方格地图”为起点，而是 **先按已有素材的正确使用方式组装完整地图**，再把钱包、头像、商店、传送门、MetaAI 功能作为 POI 和系统层叠加上去。

新增清单文档：
[docs/complete-map-assets.md](/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/GameGmeta/docs/complete-map-assets.md)

已列出的主要完整地图素材：

- `kenney-rpg-urban-pack`：现代城市街区，适合主城大厅、钱包广场、头像市场、创作者商店。
- `kenney-tiny-town`：小镇/村庄地图，适合新手社交 hub。
- `kenney-rpg-base`：RPG 户外城镇/湖泊/路径，适合城镇边缘和任务区。
- `kenney-map-pack`：世界路线图，适合章节/传送目的地选择，不适合作为走路地图。
- `kenney-sci-fi-rts`：科幻殖民地/资源基地，适合 Event Portal 目标地图。
- `kenney-tower-defense-top-down`：塔防路线场景，适合活动副本或小游戏。
- 全量库里还有 `kenney-tiny-dungeon`、`kenney-pico-8-city`、`kenney-1-bit-pack`、`kenney-monochrome-pirates` 等带 TMX/sample 的完整地图候选。

function loop(now) {

window.addEventListener("resize", resize);

});
window.addEventListener("keyup", (event) => keys.delete(event.code));

document.querySelectorAll(".wallet-strip button").forEach((button) => {

    const text = {

    message.textContent = text;
    sidePanel.innerHTML = `<strong>${button.textContent}</strong><p>${text}</p>`;
  });
});

async function start() {
  await Promise.all(Object.entries(assets).map(([key, src]) => loadImage(key, src)));

  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}

start().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  message.textContent = `素材加载失败：${error.message}`;
});

:root {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --bg: #061017;

  --muted: #8eb2c3;

* {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

html,
body {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  margin: 0;

}

}

#game {

  image-rendering: pixelated;
}

  position: absolute;

}

}

}

}

button {

}

}

}

}

.action-panel {

}

#message {

  font-weight: 720;
}

.controls {
  margin-top: 8px;

.side-panel {

@media (max-width: 760px) {

 GameGmeta is a lightweight 2D metaverse prototype focused on map-based social
 interaction and MetaAI-assisted world building.
 
-Players enter a top-down virtual city, move between districts, inspect land
-plots, open wallet/inventory panels, react with emotes, and interact with
-portals that connect city, space, and event zones.
+Players enter complete, authored pixel maps built from the downloaded CC0
+asset packs. The project should not start from a generic metaverse square grid.
+Each scene should first respect the intended use of its source pack: city
+streets are assembled as streets and buildings, tiny-town assets become a
+village hub, sci-fi RTS assets become a colony/event zone, and world-map assets
+become route selection rather than walkable ground.
+
+MetaAI features are layered on top of these finished maps as interaction
+systems: NPC guidance, room/shop generation, land descriptions, quest prompts,
+and portal destinations.

@@ -21,6 +31,20 @@ portals that connect city, space, and event zones.

+## Map Assembly Rule
+
+The map design rule is: complete-map-first, platform-second.
+
+- Do not represent the world as abstract square plots unless the source pack is
+  actually a grid/land overview pack.
+- Build maps from the visual grammar shown in each pack's `Sample.png` or TMX

+- Treat wallet, avatar, shop, and portal functions as labels or interactive

  { name: "Creator Shops", x: 34 * TILE, y: 8 * TILE, color: "#75e28f", text: "Creator Shops：后续可以接入 AI 生成房间、商店和道具。" },
  { name: "Event Portal", x: 36 * TILE, y: 22 * TILE, color: "#<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="2032" />h.floor(window.innerWidth);
  camera.height = Math.floor(window.innerHeight);
  canvas.width = Math.floor(window.innerWidth * ratio);
  canvas.height = Math.floor(window.innerHeight * ratio);
  canvas.style.width = `${window.innerWidth}px`;
  canvas.style.height = `${window.innerHeight}px`;
  ctx.setTransform(ratio, 0, 0, ratio, 0, 0);
  ctx.imageSmoothingEnabled = false;
}

function loop(now) {
  const dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - lastTime) / 1000);
  lastTime = now;
  update(dt);
  drawWorld();
  drawMinimap();
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}

window.addEventListener("resize", resize);
window.addEventListener("keydown", (event) => {
  keys.add(event.code);
  if (event.code === "KeyE") interact();
});
window.addEventListener("keyup", (event) => keys.delete(event.code));

document.querySelectorAll(".wallet-strip button").forEach((button) => {
  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    document.querySelectorAll(".wallet-strip button").forEach((item) => item.classList.remove("active"));
    button.classList.add("active");
    const panel = button.dataset.panel;
    const text = {
      wallet: "Wallet：这里后续接入资产、通行证、角色物品和交易记录。",
      avatar: "Avatar：切换形状角色、机器人助手和表情动作。",
      build: "Build：用 MetaAI 生成房间、地块和创作者商店。",
      portal: "Portal：进入科幻活动区、星球地图和限时事件。",
    }[panel];
    message.textContent = text;
    sidePanel.innerHTML = `<strong>${button.textContent}</strong><p>${text}</p>`;
  });
});

async function start() {
  await Promise.all(Object.entries(assets).map(([key, src]) => loadImage(key, src)));
  resize();
  message.textContent = "元宇宙地图已加载：先探索 Wallet Plaza、Avatar Market、Creator Shops 和 Event Portal。";
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}

start().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  message.textContent = `素材加载失败：${error.message}`;
});

+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var image := Image.new()
+	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
+	var texture: Texture2D = null
+	if err == OK:
+		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
+	else:
+		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
+		if texture == null:
+			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture

-GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.

-The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into

+The current project goal is narrow: convert curated Kenney CC0 map references
+into playable Godot `TileSet` + `TileMapLayer` maps with physical boundaries and

@@
 ## Current Prototype
 
-The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` builds a playable 2D metaverse pixel map
-at runtime from the selected Kenney CC0 assets. It now follows the Godot map
-production path:
+The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` starts with map selection cards. Each card
+enters a generated playable map based on one reference image:
+
+- Modern City Hub
+- Tiny Village Hub
+- World Route Map
+- Sci-Fi Colony
+- Tower Event Map
+
+The implementation follows the Godot map production path:
 
 - Kenney PNG tilesheets are loaded into a programmatic Godot `TileSet`.
 - `TileSetAtlasSource` slices the urban, tiny-town, and sci-fi tilesheets.
-- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, roads, buildings, and blocked boundary tiles.
-- The `TileSet` physics layer marks border, building, and sci-fi obstacle tiles as collidable.
-- The avatar is a `CharacterBody2D` with a collision shape and `move_and_slide()`.
-
-It includes:
-
-- city lobby and roads
-- wallet plaza
-- avatar market
-- creator shops
-- sci-fi event portal
-- land-grid preview
-- minimap, HUD, and wallet dock
-- movable avatar with `WASD` / arrow-key input and `E` interactions
+- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, routes, buildings, water, and blocked tiles.
+- The `TileSet` physics layer marks wall, water, building, tree, rock, and machine tiles as collidable.
+- The avatar is an animated roguelike character `CharacterBody2D` with a collision shape and `move_and_slide()`.
+- `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.
@@
-Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and add the `Web` preset.
-The intended export target is `exports/web/`, so the exported Godot build can be
-served next to the existing browser prototype when the map is ready for testing.
+Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and the `Web` preset.
+The intended export target is `exports/web/`.

+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var image := Image.new()
+	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
+	var texture: Texture2D = null
+	if err == OK:
+		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
+	else:
+		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
+		if texture == null:
+			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture

-GameGmeta is a local MetaAI / metaverse game project scaffold.
+GameGmeta is a local Godot map-building prototype.
 
-The first project goal is to turn the curated CC0 metaverse UI asset series into
-a usable 2D virtual-world prototype: city map, land plots, avatar/social UI,
-wallet/inventory panels, minimap navigation, and portal effects.
+The current project goal is narrow: convert curated Kenney CC0 map references
+into playable Godot `TileSet` + `TileMapLayer` maps with physical boundaries and
+one animated `CharacterBody2D` player.
@@
 ## Current Prototype
 
-The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` builds a playable 2D metaverse pixel map
-at runtime from the selected Kenney CC0 assets. It now follows the Godot map
-production path:
+The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` starts with map selection cards. Each card
+enters a generated playable map based on one reference image:
+
+- Modern City Hub
+- Tiny Village Hub
+- World Route Map
+- Sci-Fi Colony
+- Tower Event Map
+
+The implementation follows the Godot map production path:
 
 - Kenney PNG tilesheets are loaded into a programmatic Godot `TileSet`.
 - `TileSetAtlasSource` slices the urban, tiny-town, and sci-fi tilesheets.
-- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, roads, buildings, and blocked boundary tiles.
-- The `TileSet` physics layer marks border, building, and sci-fi obstacle tiles as collidable.
-- The avatar is a `CharacterBody2D` with a collision shape and `move_and_slide()`.
-
-It includes:
-
-- city lobby and roads
-- wallet plaza
-- avatar market
-- creator shops
-- sci-fi event portal
-- land-grid preview
-- minimap, HUD, and wallet dock
-- movable avatar with `WASD` / arrow-key input and `E` interactions
+- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, routes, buildings, water, and blocked tiles.
+- The `TileSet` physics layer marks wall, water, building, tree, rock, and machine tiles as collidable.
+- The avatar is an animated roguelike character `CharacterBody2D` with a collision shape and `move_and_slide()`.
+- `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.
@@
-Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and add the `Web` preset.
-The intended export target is `exports/web/`, so the exported Godot build can be
-served next to the existing browser prototype when the map is ready for testing.
+Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and the `Web` preset.
+The intended export target is `exports/web/`.
*** End Patch

func _create_atlas_source(path: String, coords: Array[Vector2i]) -> TileSetAtlasSource:
	var source := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
	source.texture = _texture(path)
	source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE)
	source.separation = Vector2i(ATLAS_SPACING, ATLAS_SPACING)
	for coord in coords:
		source.create_tile(coord)
	return source

func _add_collision_to_tile(set: TileSet, source_id: int, coord: Vector2i) -> void:
	var source := set.get_source(source_id) as TileSetAtlasSource
	var tile_data := source.get_tile_data(coord, 0)
	if tile_data == null:
		return
	tile_data.add_collision_polygon(0)
	tile_data.set_collision_polygon_points(0, 0, PackedVector2Array([

		Vector2(SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE),

func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
	if atlas_cache.has(key):
		return atlas_cache[key]
	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
	tex.region = region
	tex.filter_clip = true
	atlas_cache[key] = tex
	return tex

func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
	if atlas_cache.has(path):
		return atlas_cache[path]
	var image := Image.new()
	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
	var texture: Texture2D = null
	if err == OK:
		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
	else:
		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
		if texture == null:
			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
	atlas_cache[path] = texture
	return texture

func _create_atlas_source(path: String, coords: Array[Vector2i]) -> TileSetAtlasSource:
	var source := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
	source.texture = _texture(path)
	source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE)
	source.separation = Vector2i(ATLAS_SPACING, ATLAS_SPACING)
	for coord in coords:
		source.create_tile(coord)
	return source

func _add_collision_to_tile(set: TileSet, source_id: int, coord: Vector2i) -> void:
	var source := set.get_source(source_id) as TileSetAtlasSource
	var tile_data := source.get_tile_data(coord, 0)
	if tile_data == null:
		return
	tile_data.add_collision_polygon(0)
	tile_data.set_collision_polygon_points(0, 0, PackedVector2Array([
		Vector2(0, 0),
		Vector2(SOURCE_TILE, 0),
		Vector2(SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE),
		Vector2(0, SOURCE_TILE),
	]))

func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
	if atlas_cache.has(key):
		return atlas_cache[key]
	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
	tex.region = region
	tex.filter_clip = true
	atlas_cache[key] = tex
	return tex

func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
	if atlas_cache.has(path):
		return atlas_cache[path]
	var image := Image.new()
	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
	var texture: Texture2D = null
	if err == OK:
		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
	else:
		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
		if texture == null:
			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
	atlas_cache[path] = texture
	return texture

改动重点：

  - 世界路线：岛屿、水域物理边界、路线节点。
  - 科幻殖民地：基地道路、设施、岩石/机器障碍。
  - 塔防地图：路径、河道、沙地、炮塔/障碍。
- 角色改为 `Puny-Characters/Warrior-Blue.png`，这是 32x32 网格的完整动作表，脚本中按 `walk_down/up/left/right` 播放。
- `TileSet` 里继续给墙、水、建筑、树、岩石、机器类 tile 设置 Physics Layer。
- `CharacterBody2D` 使用 `move_and_slide()` 移动。
- 已保留 Godot Web 导出 preset。

func _clear_scene() -> void:

		ui_layer.queue_free()

	player = null
	player_sprite = null

	bg.size = Vector2(MAP_W * TILE + 520, MAP_H * TILE + 340)

func _create_tile_layer(layer_name: String, z: int) -> TileMapLayer:
	var layer := TileMapLayer.new()

	layer.tile_set = tile_set
	layer.scale = Vector2(2, 2)
	layer.z_index = z
	map_root.add_child(layer)
	return layer

func _create_atlas_source(path: String, coords: Array[Vector2i]) -> TileSetAtlasSource:
	var source := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
	source.texture = _texture(path)
	source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(SOURCE_TILE, SOURCE_TILE)
	source.separation = Vector2i(ATLAS_SPACING, ATLAS_SPACING)
	for coord in coords:
		source.create_tile(coord)
	return source

func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
	if atlas_cache.has(key):
		return atlas_cache[key]
	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
	tex.region = region
	tex.filter_clip = true
	atlas_cache[key] = tex
	return tex

func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
	if atlas_cache.has(path):
		return atlas_cache[path]
	var image := Image.new()
	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
	var texture: Texture2D = null
	if err == OK:
		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
	else:
		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
		if texture == null:
			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
	atlas_cache[path] = texture
	return texture

	if atlas_cache.has(key):

	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()

	tex.region = region
	tex.filter_clip = true
	atlas_cache[key] = tex
	return tex

func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
	if atlas_cache.has(path):
		return atlas_cache[path]
	var image := Image.new()
	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
	var texture: Texture2D = null
	if err == OK:
		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
	else:
		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
		if texture == null:
			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
	atlas_cache[path] = texture
	return texture

-The implementation follows the Godot map production path:
+The implementation now follows a reference-map-first Godot production path:
 
-- Kenney PNG tilesheets are loaded into a programmatic Godot `TileSet`.
-- `TileSetAtlasSource` slices the urban, tiny-town, and sci-fi tilesheets.
-- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, routes, buildings, water, and blocked tiles.
-- The `TileSet` physics layer marks wall, water, building, tree, rock, and machine tiles as collidable.
+- Each complete reference map PNG is sliced into 16 x 16 cells as a Godot `TileSetAtlasSource`.
+- One `TileMapLayer` redraws the full reference map from those TileSet cells, preserving the original map style.
+- Map-specific blocked cells are written back into the reference `TileSet` physics layer.
+- The same blocked cells also generate hidden `StaticBody2D` boundaries, so building/water/tree/rock collision is explicit in play.
 - The avatar uses `assets/game/avatars/puny_warrior_blue.png`, a 32px-grid character sheet with directional walk frames, inside an animated `CharacterBody2D`.
 - `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.
*** End Patch

+func _atlas_custom(path: String, region: Rect2) -> AtlasTexture:
+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):
+		return atlas_cache[key]
+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)
+	tex.region = region
+	tex.filter_clip = true
+	atlas_cache[key] = tex
+	return tex
+
+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var image := Image.new()
+	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
+	var texture: Texture2D = null
+	if err == OK:
+		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
+	else:
+		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
+		if texture == null:
+			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture
+	return texture

-The implementation follows the Godot map production path:
+The implementation now follows a reference-map-first Godot production path:
 
-- Kenney PNG tilesheets are loaded into a programmatic Godot `TileSet`.
-- `TileSetAtlasSource` slices the urban, tiny-town, and sci-fi tilesheets.
-- `TileMapLayer` nodes draw ground, routes, buildings, water, and blocked tiles.
-- The `TileSet` physics layer marks wall, water, building, tree, rock, and machine tiles as collidable.
+- Each complete reference map PNG is sliced into 16 x 16 cells as a Godot `TileSetAtlasSource`.
+- One `TileMapLayer` redraws the full reference map from those TileSet cells, preserving the original map style.
+- Map-specific blocked cells are written back into the reference `TileSet` physics layer.
+- The same blocked cells also generate hidden `StaticBody2D` boundaries, so building/water/tree/rock collision is explicit in play.
 - The avatar uses `assets/game/avatars/puny_warrior_blue.png`, a 32px-grid character sheet with directional walk frames, inside an animated `CharacterBody2D`.
 - `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.
*** End Patch

+	var key := "%s:%s" % [path, region]
+	if atlas_cache.has(key):

+	var tex := AtlasTexture.new()
+	tex.atlas = _texture(path)

+	atlas_cache[key] = tex

+func _texture(path: String) -> Texture2D:
+	if atlas_cache.has(path):
+		return atlas_cache[path]
+	var image := Image.new()
+	var err := image.load(ProjectSettings.globalize_path(path))
+	var texture: Texture2D = null
+	if err == OK:
+		texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)
+	else:
+		texture = load(path) as Texture2D
+		if texture == null:
+			push_error("Missing texture: " + path)
+	atlas_cache[path] = texture

# GameGmeta

GameGmeta is a local Godot map-building prototype.

The current project goal is narrow: convert curated Kenney CC0 map references
into playable Godot `TileSet` + `TileMapLayer` maps with physical boundaries and
one animated `CharacterBody2D` player.

## Project Structure

- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
- `assets/game`: imported first-pass Godot runtime assets for the prototype.
- `assets/licenses`: CC0 license files copied with the runtime assets.
- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
- `scenes`: Godot scenes.
- `scripts`: Godot gameplay and UI scripts.
- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.

## Local Asset Source

The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:

`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`

This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
runtime asset pipeline are fixed.

## Run The Godot Prototype

From this folder:

```bash
HOME=/private/tmp/godot-home /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/tools/godot4 --path /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/GameGmeta
```

Script check:

```bash
HOME=/private/tmp/godot-home /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/tools/godot4 --headless --path /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/GameGmeta --check-only --script scripts/main.gd
```

VSCode task files are in `.vscode/`.

## Current Prototype

The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` starts with map selection cards. Each card
enters a generated playable map based on one reference image:

- Modern City Hub
- Tiny Village Hub
- World Route Map
- Sci-Fi Colony
- Tower Event Map

The implementation now follows a reference-map-first Godot production path:

- Each complete r<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="5" />`TileSetAtlasSource`.
- One `TileMapLayer` redraws the full reference map from those TileSet cells, preserving the original map style.
- Map-specific blocked cells are written back into the reference `TileSet` physics layer.
- The same blocked cells also generate hidden `StaticBody2D` boundaries, so building/water/tree/rock collision is explicit in play.
- The avatar uses `assets/game/avatars/puny_warrior_blue.png`, a 32px-grid character sheet with directional walk frames, inside an animated `CharacterBody2D`.
- `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.

## Godot Web Export Path

Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and the `Web` preset.
The intended export target is `exports/web/`.

## Run The Web Prototype

The browser version lives in `web/` and loads the same curated runtime assets.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8787
```

Then open:

`http://127.0.0.1:8787/web/index.html`

The Web prototype includes canvas-rendered city/portal map loading, keyboard
movement, minimap, wallet/avatar/build/portal HUD buttons, and district
interaction prompts.

It now starts with map cards for complete map scenes:

- Modern City Hub
- Tiny Village Hub
- World Route Map
- Sci-Fi Colony
- Tower Event

Use the `Maps` HUD button or `Escape` to return to the map selection cards.

## Core Visual Direction

Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:

- modern city and small town maps
- world/land overview maps
- simple avatar and robot NPCs
- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
- minimap and input prompts
- portal, reward, and lighting effects

Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.

## Planning Docs

- `docs/product-brief.md`: current game direction and MVP rules.
- `docs/complete-map-assets.md`: complete-map asset inventory and revised map strategy.
- `docs/asset-usage.md`: asset source and import rules.

# Browser

Use this skill for browser automation tasks such as inspecting pages, navigating, testing local apps, clicking, typing, taking screenshots, and reading visible page state. After setup, select the `iab` browser.

Keep browser work in the background by default.

Show the browser when the user's request is primarily to put a page in front of them or let them watch the interaction, such as "open localhost:3000", "go to the docs page", "take me to the PR", "show me the current tab", or "keep the browser open while you test checkout".

Do not show the browser when navigation is only a means to answer a question or verify behavior, such as "check localhost:3000 and tell me whether login works", "inspect the docs page and summarize what changed", or "verify the modal still opens correctly". Localhost targets and ordinary page navigation do not by themselves require visibility.

When the browser should be visible to the user, actually present it with `await (await browser.capabilities.get("visibility")).set(true)`.

If this plugin is listed as available in the session, treat that as mandatory reading before browser work. Open and follow this skill before saying that Browser is unavailable and before falling back to standalone Playwright or Computer Use.

Do not skip this skill just because Computer Use MCP tool calls are directly visible or appear easier to invoke. The presence of Computer Use tools is not evidence that Computer Use is the preferred browser surface.

Before using this skill for the first time in the current conversation context, read<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="2463" />cell that never created the binding.

### General guidance

* Minimize interruptions as much as possible. Only ask clarifying questions if you really need to. If a user has an under-specified prompt, try to fulfill it first before asking for more information.
* Remember, the user is asking questions about what they see on the screen. Base your interactions on what is visible to the user (based on DOM and screenshots) rather than programmatically determining what they are talking about. The "first link" on the page is not necessarily the first `a href` in the DOM.
* Try not to over-complicate things. It is okay to click based on node ID if it is not clear how to determine the UI element in Playwright.
* If a tab is already on a given URL, do not call `goto` with the same URL. This will reload the page and may lose any in-progress information the user has provided. When you intentionally need to reload, call `tab.reload()`.
* If browser-use is interrupted because the extension or user took control, do not quote the raw runtime error. Summarize it naturally for the user, for example: "Browser use was stopped in the extension." Avoid internal terms like turn_id, runtime, retry, or plugin error text unless the user asks for details.
* When testing a user's local app on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or another local development URL in a framework that does not support hot reloading or hot reloading is disabled, call `tab.reload()` after code or build changes before verifying the UI. After reloading, take a fresh DOM snapshot or screenshot before continuing.
* Do not brute-force undocumented site search URLs, query parameter variants, search engine query grids, or candidate URL arrays unless the user explicitly asks for exhaustive coverage.
* If a guessed URL, search query, or candidate page fails, try at most one new approach. After that, switch to visible page navigation, the site's own search UI, or give the best current answer with uncertainty.

# GameGmeta

GameGmeta is a local Godot map-building prototype.

The current project goal is narrow: convert curated Kenney CC0 map references
into playable Godot `TileSet` + `TileMapLayer` maps with physical boundaries and
one animated `CharacterBody2D` player.

## Project Structure

- `assets/manifests`: selected asset catalog and source notes.
- `assets/game`: imported first-pass Godot runtime assets for the prototype.
- `assets/licenses`: CC0 license files copied with the runtime assets.
- `docs`: product direction, asset usage rules, and implementation notes.
- `prototypes`: quick experiments and throwaway playable tests.
- `scenes`: Godot scenes.
- `scripts`: Godot gameplay and UI scripts.
- `src`: production source code when the app/game stack is chosen.

## Local Asset Source

The curated source asset folder is outside this repo for now:

`/Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/metaverse-ui-assets`

This repo keeps the selected manifest in Git, but does not copy all image files
yet. That avoids committing thousands of binary files before the engine and
runtime asset pipeline are fixed.

## Run The Godot Prototype

From this folder:

```bash
HOME=/private/tmp/godot-home /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/tools/godot4 --path /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/GameGmeta
```

Script check:

```bash
HOME=/private/tmp/godot-home /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/tools/godot4 --headless --path /Users/vincet/Documents/aiglass/GameGmeta --check-only --script scripts/main.gd
```

VSCode task files are in `.vscode/`.

## Current Prototype

The first scene at `scenes/main.tscn` starts with map selection cards. Each card
enters a generated playable map based on one reference image:

- Modern City Hub
- Tiny Village Hub
- World Route Map
- Sci-Fi Colony
- Tower Event Map

The implementation now follows a reference-map-first Godot production path:

- Each complete r<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="5" />`TileSetAtlasSource`.
- One `TileMapLayer` redraws the full reference map from those TileSet cells, preserving the original map style.
- Map-specific blocked cells are written back into the reference `TileSet` physics layer.
- The same blocked cells also generate hidden `StaticBody2D` boundaries, so building/water/tree/rock collision is explicit in play.
- The avatar uses `assets/game/avatars/puny_warrior_blue.png`, a 32px-grid character sheet with directional walk frames, inside an animated `CharacterBody2D`.
- `WASD` / arrow keys move; `Esc` or `Maps` returns to card selection.

## Godot Web Export Path

Open the project in Godot, then use `Project > Export` and the `Web` preset.
The intended export target is `exports/web/`.

## Run The Web Prototype

The browser version lives in `web/` and loads the same curated runtime assets.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8787
```

Then open:

`http://127.0.0.1:8787/web/index.html`

The Web prototype includes canvas-rendered city/portal map loading, keyboard
movement, minimap, wallet/avatar/build/portal HUD buttons, and district
interaction prompts.

It now starts with map cards for complete map scenes:

- Modern City Hub
- Tiny Village Hub
- World Route Map
- Sci-Fi Colony
- Tower Event

Use the `Maps` HUD button or `Escape` to return to the map selection cards.

## Core Visual Direction

Use the Kenney CC0 top-down/tiny-world style as the main visual language:

- modern city and small town maps
- world/land overview maps
- simple avatar and robot NPCs
- sci-fi wallet and HUD panels
- minimap and input prompts
- portal, reward, and lighting effects

Avoid mixing in 1-bit, monochrome, sketch, scribble, card, puzzle, and platformer
packs unless they are used as separate themed zones.

## Planning Docs

- `docs/product-brief.md`: current game direction and MVP rules.
- `docs/complete-map-assets.md`: complete-map asset inventory and revised map strategy.
- `docs/asset-usage.md`: asset source and import rules.
